core_obligations: Choose the w-local diagram (proof lines 1808-1818): a weakly etale A -> B induces algebraic extensions of residue fields, so the residue field lemma applies and produces a diagram B -> D over A -> C with w-local spectra, closed points conditions and strictly henselian local rings at maximal ideals.

Show that C -> D identifies local rings (proof lines 1818-1826): the map C -> D is weakly etale by permanence; a maximal ideal m of D lies over a maximal ideal m' of C, and rigidity of weakly etale maps between strictly henselian local rings makes C_{m'} -> D_m an isomorphism; since every point of Spec(C) specializes to a closed point, C -> D identifies local rings.

Finish (proof lines 1826-1831): the local isomorphism proposition applies to C -> D, giving a faithfully flat ind-Zariski D -> D' such that C -> D' is ind-Zariski; then B -> D' is faithfully flat and ind-etale and A -> D' is ind-etale, which is the required solution.
proof_roadmap: Use the residue field input to enter the w-local diagram with strictly henselian local rings.
Deduce that the map between the middle and the top of the diagram identifies local rings via rigidity of weakly etale maps between strictly henselian local rings.
Apply the local isomorphism proposition to make the whole square ind-Zariski over the source.
difficulty_reason: The proposition proves that for a weakly etale ring map A -> B there is a faithfully flat ind-etale B -> B' with A -> B' ind-etale (statement lines 1801-1806). The proof (proof lines 1808-1834) passes to a diagram with w-local spectra and strictly henselian local rings, shows that the map between the middle and top identifies local rings using rigidity of weakly etale maps between strictly henselian local rings, and applies the local isomorphism proposition. H2: a three-step reduction with four inputs, written out in full.
